Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

phylogp 0.2.0

  • kernel_equivalent() checks whether one kernel can reproduce the tip distribution of another: for each parameter setting of the first it searches over all parameters of the second for the smallest Kullback-Leibler divergence, comparing contrasts when the mean is unknown. It flags best-fitting parameters that sit at their bounds.

  • phylo_gp_trees() fits a model across a sample of trees and pools the posterior (or collects maximum-likelihood estimates), reporting how much of the uncertainty comes from the phylogeny; loo() works on the pooled fit.

  • loo_group() does leave-clade-out (or any leave-group-out) cross-validation: refits without each group and scores the group’s joint predictive density, in linear time for branch-wise kernels. Returns a kfold object for loo::loo_compare().

  • Tree matrices (incidence, shared path lengths, distances) are cached per tree_info() object.

  • predict() gives posterior predictions for fitted species and for species in the tree without data (kriging on the tree).

  • ancestral() reconstructs ancestral states in linear time; for OU it uses the OU process itself rather than its tip kernel.

  • loo_refit() replaces the PSIS-LOO contribution of influential species (high Pareto k) by an exact refit.

  • Varying slopes: k_slope(x) * k_bm() (or another branch-wise kernel) for slopes that evolve along the tree, fitted with latent node values in linear time or with the dense marginal kernel; k_slope(x) * k_white() as the heteroscedastic control. varying_slopes() summarises the slopes.

  • k_white(df = ): Student-t residuals for data with outlying species.

  • Leave-one-out integrates each species’ own latent values (slopes, rates, variance multipliers); k_relaxed() can now be combined with dense components.

  • plot_tree_values() colours a tree by any value.

  • New vignette: “Slopes, prediction and robust residuals”.

phylogp 0.1.0

  • First version.
  • Kernel grammar: classical kernels (k_bm(), k_lambda(), k_kappa(), k_delta(), k_eb(), k_ou(), k_white()), extensions (k_relaxed(), k_rate_time(), k_dist()) and user-defined branch-wise kernels (k_edge()), combined with +.
  • phylo_gp() writes, compiles and fits the Stan program by maximum likelihood or HMC, with an O(N) pruning likelihood and O(N) leave-one-out densities for branch-wise kernels.
  • Design tools: kernel_check(), kernel_plot(), kernel_matrix(), kernel_simulate(), kernel_loglik(), make_stancode().
  • Rate summaries: edge_rates(), plot_edge_rates(), plot_tree_rates(), rate_through_time().
  • Vignettes: “Getting started with phylogp” and “Designing kernels”.
